# Florence 1347 – Tools, machines & manufacturing

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Pulleys, block and tackle, treadwheel crane** [`block_and_tackle`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/block_and_tackle.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Treadwheel hoists and pulley blocks lift stone on the cathedral and bell-tower sites. Loads go straight up; no reversible gear or load-positioning crane exists. Local: Opera del Duomo (campanile begun by Giotto in 1334, still rising); builders of the Orsanmichele grain loggia.
- **Wheelbarrow** [`wheelbarrow`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wheelbarrow.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high
- **Archimedes' screw (water screw)** [`archimedes_screw`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/archimedes_screw.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept high. A name in Vitruvius, which hardly anyone has read. Drainage and irrigation use buckets, scoop wheels and chains of pots. Local: coopers and carpenters.
- **Gears and gear trains** [`gears_gear_trains`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gears_gear_trains.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Mills use wooden peg wheels and lantern pinions. Filed iron clock wheels are a new art found in Milan and Padua, not here. No theory of tooth shape. Local: millwrights. Elsewhere: Padua, Jacopo Dondi's clock (1344); Milan.
- **Cam and camshaft** [`cam_camshaft`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cam_camshaft.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high Local: fulling mills on the Arno; paper mills of Fabriano.
- **Screw, nut and bolt** [`screw_nut_bolt`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/screw_nut_bolt.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Big wooden screws, cut by hand, work oil, wine and cloth presses. Metal screws as fasteners are not made; smiths join with rivets, wedges and pins. Local: press makers; cloth finishers.
- **Belt, rope and chain drives** [`belt_drive`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/belt_drive.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Cord bands drive spinning wheels and turners' and gem cutters' wheels. Flat leather belts on shafting and link chains for power are unknown.
- **Ball and roller bearings** [`ball_bearings`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ball_bearings.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Axles run in greased wood, bronze or iron. Wooden rollers are easy; hard, truly round metal balls of equal size are not.
- **Bellows and the double-acting piston blower** [`bellows_piston_blower`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bellows_piston_blower.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Leather bellows are standard, worked by hand or foot and by water wheels at some ironworks. The double-acting wooden piston box is unknown. Local: ironworks smelting Elba ore on the Pisan coast and in the Pistoia hills; bell founders. Elsewhere: China, double-acting box bellows.
- **Water-powered trip hammer and stamp mill** [`trip_hammer_water_powered`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/trip_hammer_water_powered.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high Local: fulling mills (gualchiere) on the Arno; iron hammer mills (magli); paper stamp mills of Fabriano.
- **Lost-wax casting** [`lost_wax_casting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lost_wax_casting.md) — K3, use correct, make medium, accept high. Goldsmiths and bell founders cast well, but for the Baptistery's bronze doors (1330-1336) a Venetian founder had to be fetched. Large fine casts are a risk. Local: Andrea Pisano's Baptistery doors; goldsmiths; bell founders. Elsewhere: Venice, bronze founders.
- **Sand and loam moulding for large castings** [`sand_loam_casting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sand_loam_casting.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Bells are cast in loam moulds built for one pour; in 1326 the Signoria ordered its first small metal cannon. Reusable sand flasks and cast iron are unknown. Local: bell founders.
- **Wire drawing** [`wire_drawing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wire_drawing.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Wire is drawn by hand through iron drawplates, piece by piece. No water-powered wire mill exists anywhere yet. Local: goldsmiths; mail makers and needle makers.
- **Rolling and slitting mill** [`rolling_mill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/rolling_mill.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Sheet metal and florin blanks are hammered. Small rolls for gold or lead are makeable; true cylindrical rolls and a stiff frame are the difficulty. Local: the Zecca (mint); goldsmiths; goldbeaters.
- **Precision cylinder boring** [`boring_machine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/boring_machine.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. The few cannon are small cast or forged pots, used as cast. Wooden water pipes are bored with augers; a guided boring bar for metal is new. Local: bell founders; carpenters (pipe augers).
- **Screw-cutting lathe with slide rest** [`lathe_screw_cutting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lathe_screw_cutting.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept high. Turners use pole and bow lathes that spin back and forth, the tool held by hand. Nobody has a lead screw or tool slide. Local: wood turners; pewterers.
- **Precision measurement (flat surfaces, gauges, micrometer)** [`precision_measurement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/precision_measurement.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. Parts are fitted to each other by eye, dividers and callipers. Every city has its own braccio; there are no gauges or flat reference plates.
- **Machine tools (planer, shaper, milling machine)** [`machine_tools`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/machine_tools.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept medium
- **Interchangeable parts** [`interchangeable_parts`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/interchangeable_parts.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Every lock, crossbow nut and hinge is fitted to its neighbour by hand. Guild cloth standards fix sizes of goods, not of parts. Elsewhere: Venice Arsenal, galleys built to common patterns.
- **Assembly line and mass production** [`assembly_line`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/assembly_line.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. The wool trade splits work into dozens of steps across homes and shops. The guild forbids workers to organise: Ciuto Brandini was hanged for it in 1345. Local: Arte della Lana (some 200 workshops by Villani's count); Arte di Calimala. Elsewhere: Venice Arsenal.
- **Water-powered sawmill** [`sawmill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sawmill.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. Timber is pit-sawn by two men; Casentino firs come down the Arno by raft. A millwright who knows fulling-mill cams can build a water saw. Local: Opera del Duomo's timber supply from the Casentino; pit sawyers. Elsewhere: Augsburg (sawmill recorded 1322); northern France.
- **Spinning wheel** [`spinning_wheel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spinning_wheel.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The great wheel is a few generations old and trusted only for soft weft; warp must be spun on the distaff. No flyer, no treadle. Local: lanaioli (wool merchants) and their spinners in the contado.
- **Spinning machines (jenny, water frame, mule)** [`spinning_machines`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spinning_machines.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. Silk is twisted on circular throwing mills with many spindles, a Lucchese secret carried abroad by exiles. Nothing similar exists for wool, which feeds thousands of spinners. Local: Lucchese silk workers in Florence; Arte di Por Santa Maria. Elsewhere: Lucca; Bologna, water-driven silk mills.
- **Horizontal treadle loom** [`treadle_loom`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/treadle_loom.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high Local: wool weavers (broadloom, two men); a few silk weavers.
- **Flying shuttle and power loom** [`power_loom`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/power_loom.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. A flying shuttle is carpenter's work; a powered loom is far harder. Weavers are poor dependants of the guild merchants and fear for their bread.
- **Cotton gin** [`cotton_gin`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cotton_gin.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Cotton arrives already cleaned, in bales from Syria and Cyprus via Venice and Genoa, for Lombard fustian. No one in Tuscany handles seed cotton. Elsewhere: India and the Levant, roller gins.
- **Stocking frame (knitting machine)** [`knitting_frame`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/knitting_frame.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Hose are cut and sewn from woven cloth; hand knitting on needles is known. A frame needs hundreds of identical fine sprung hooks.
